body:
We used an offline VM running a copy of our Agie Classic Cut 2S machine control. We imported CAMCraft’s ISO, SBR and SBL for the 40 × 20 mm punch. FORMALCHECK reported zero job errors with setup, reference and option warnings. GRAFICHECK showed four outward passes and the 1 mm separation. See #2999 for the later test of a conflicting saved quality and the corrected import workflow.

All controller runs were offline. No physical cut was made.

@qsmits thank you for the careful work and the clear PR body.

## What looks good

- The writer refuses before it creates any output. The checks are: machine model and kind, one operation, one mount and setup, default post options, millimetre document, empty program number and comment, the AGIE_QN2 condition row (role rough, wire 0.25 mm, preview gap 0.005), no stated stock material, no tank or flushing mode, no stops or coolant override, the first work offset without rotation or flip, own box stock, no fixtures, stock top at Z0, 20 mm thickness, the guide heights, one closed loop, and a closed convex vertical prism (`crates/app/src/operation/agie_profile.rs:8-131`, `crates/app/src/posting_agie.rs:26-110`).
- The coordinate origin is the setup work offset from `posting::wcs_context` (through `job.wcs_origin`). The ISO and the SBL use the same frame. There is no second derivation.
- The ISO is nominal geometry. The writer applies no wire radius and no gap. The SBL creates the work with zero erosion steps (`ASDELETE`). The operator must assign the technology on the control. The receipt (GUI status, script and MCP `posted_view`) names the required control checks. No example offset is posted as machine technology.
- Unsupported kinds are refused: taper, four-axis, tabs, burnout and skims (`agie_profile.rs:12-21`); die and open sides (only `WireSide::Punch` passes); more than one loop (`agie_profile.rs:117`); more than one model; other machines; per-operation output (`posting_per_op.rs`); more than one mount (`posting_mounts.rs`); the in-memory post (`posting.rs` `post_setup_unwritten`). Any path that runs `agie-native.cps` as a text post stops in `onOpen` with a diagnostic. This is a good safety net.
- Numeric safety: `quantize` refuses non-finite values and values above 9999.9999 mm before the `as i64` cast. `micrometres` uses `try_from` and a round-trip check. The orientation and area use `i128`. The two `round() as i64` casts in `entry_face` take values that are already in range. All index operations use `% n` with `n >= 3`, or `n == 0` skips the loop. I found no `unwrap`, `expect`, `panic!` or `unreachable!` in the new non-test code.
- Publication (`crates/post/src/agie/mod.rs:77-171`): `symlink_metadata` refuses an existing path (a dangling link too). The three files are written with `create_new` and `sync_all` into a `tempfile` directory in the same parent. Then a rename that cannot replace publishes them: `renameat_with(..., RenameFlags::NOREPLACE)` (rustix, Linux and Apple) or `MoveFileW` without `MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING` (windows-sys). Each file handle closes before the rename. An error before the rename drops the `TempDir`, which removes the staged files. Other platforms get a clean "unavailable" error. The second post to the same name is refused and the first files stay unchanged (tested).
- File names: `valid_stem` accepts only 1 to 8 uppercase letters or digits that start with a letter. It refuses CON, AUX, NUL, PRN, COM0-9 and LPT0-9. Thus `..`, separators and long names cannot occur. The output is ASCII with CRLF, and `.gitattributes` keeps the golden bytes.
- Tests are in the correct crates, the goldens are add-only, no snapshot PNG changed, and no existing test is weaker. The `plasma_post_refusals` change moves the `post_serves` assertion up, so it now applies to every post.

## Hand trace (smallest fixture: `the_native_files_match_the_control_checked_rectangular_punch`)

- Input: punch X -20..20, Y -10..10, Z 0..20. Stock 80 x 60 x 20, so X -40..40 and Y -30..30. Work offset (0, 0, 20). Start hole (-30, 0).
- `prepare`: four corners, axis-aligned, area > 0, so the travel is counterclockwise (a clockwise ring is reversed). Stock margin: 20 mm on each face. The limit is 0.4 mm.
- `entry_face`: the left face (-20, 10) to (-20, -10). The hole is 10 mm outside it (the limit is 3 mm). t = 0.5, so the foot is (-20, 0). The foot is 10 mm from each corner (the limit is 3 mm).
- ISO: N0001 G00 X-20 Y0, N0002 X-20 Y-10, N0003 X20 Y-10, N0004 X20 Y10, N0005 X-20 Y10, N0006 X-20 Y0 (back to the entry point), N0007 M02. This agrees with `CCSEP20.ISO` for all six points. No segment has zero length.
- SBL: DIML 80.000, DIMB 60.000, POSPOSX -40.000, POSPOSY -30.000, POSPOSZ -20.000, start hole -30.000 / 0.000, diameter 2.0, SEPCUT 1.0, COMMPOINTENTRY 3.0. This agrees with `CCSEP20.SBL`.
- Translated work offset (2, 3, 20) in `the_mounted_agie_post_writes_nominal_geometry_and_preserves_existing_jobs`: X -22 / 18, Y -13 / 7, hole -32.000 / -3.000. The ISO and the SBL move together, and the Y sign does not change.

## Guards at the limit

- Stock clearance (`contour.rs:157-163`): each punch face against stock min + 0.4 mm and stock max - 0.4 mm, inclusive, in exact integer units of 0.00001 mm. Exactly 0.4 mm passes. The test uses 20.80 mm stock depth (passes), 20.60 and 20.36 (refused, the message names "0.4 mm"). The basis is 0.245 mm rough offset + 0.125 mm wire radius = 0.37 mm.
- Entry (`contour.rs:184-222`): the hole distance to the face is refused below 3 mm (exactly 3 mm passes). The foot must be at least 3 mm from each corner (inclusive). The test `start = [-30, 7]` passes at exactly 3 mm, and `[-30, 9.5]` is refused. The hole must be outside a face and within the span of that face, else the post is refused.
- The two refusal messages give the limit values (0.4 mm, 3 mm). They do not give the measured value. This is a note only.

## Blockers

None.

## Notes (not blocking)

1. `crates/app/src/posting.rs` `post_script_as`: the native branch returns before the `tracing` lines. A native success or refusal gets no "NC program written / not written" log line. Please think about one log line for each result.
2. `crates/post/src/agie/contour.rs:66`: a start hole that touches the stock edge (centre exactly 1 mm from the edge) passes. A small wall, for example 0.5 mm, can be safer. The operator can see this on the control.
3. No test sends a clockwise ring into `prepare`. The code reverses it, but one small test can pin the same ISO for the two orientations.
4. `crates/geometry/src/geometry/prism.rs:18`: a mesh above the 8,000,000 facet-side bound gives the "cavities, steps, concavities" message. That message can confuse the user for a large mesh.
5. `docs/decisions/2945-native-agie-wire.md:11` still says that the reference source is "an open review question". The maintainer decided it in comment 7079755001. A one-line update can record that.
6. The Linux and macOS rename paths are not exercised on this Windows review machine.
7. The PR adds no new undoable command. The user selects the post with the existing `SelectPost` command, and the script and MCP post receipt shows the bundle files. Thus no MCP follow-up issue is necessary.
8. Files over 400 lines: `posting.rs` (1,648), `posting_files.rs` (420), `state.rs`, `egui_app/tests.rs`, `geometry/mod.rs` and `conformance.rs`. All of them were already over the limit on main. This PR adds 1 to 14 lines to each. All new files are below 400 lines.
9. Heavy lanes: the diff touches `geometry`, `post`, `app` and `ui`, so it reaches the kernel, motion and app heavy lanes. The body says that on this head the heavy gate passed 258 of 258 steps (kernel, motion and app, base `1d5de9aeb`), and that the quick gate passed 1,079 of 1,079 steps. These are the results of the author. This review did not run them.

Hello @qsmits, thank you for this work. This is a delta review of the two new commits on top of the safety review 7079838975 (head `31ee72c80`). It is a read only. This review did not build the PR.

**Verdict: clean.** I found no blocker.

**What I checked**

- The head is `34d2863ba`. Since `31ee72c80`, the first-parent line has only `f7b27b43e` and `34d2863ba`.
- `f7b27b43e` is a merge of `main`. Its `git show --remerge-diff` is empty: there are no hand edits.
- `34d2863ba` adds one line, `sharp_corners: false,`, to the `WireContourOp` literal in `crates/app/tests/agie_native.rs` (line 97 in the file, in the literal that starts at line 84). It changes nothing else.
- `false` is the correct value. It is the default of the field from PR #3232 (`crates/app/src/operation/types/wire_edm.rs:97`): the option is off and the wire keeps the old behaviour.
- All other `WireContourOp {` literals in `crates` already state the field, or use `..` from a value that states it.

**The new option `sharp_corners: true` and the native Agie path**

Main added the option "sharp corners" (#3207) after the safety review. I read how the native path handles it:

- `agie_job` (`crates/app/src/operation/agie_profile.rs`) does not read `sharp_corners`. It refuses taper, four-axis, tabs, burnout and skims, but not this option.
- The writer gets the nominal ring (`AgieJob.contour`), not the wire-centre path. The control applies the offset. Thus the option does not change the posted files.
- The option only affects inside corners (`crates/motion/src/wire_edm/laws.rs`, `sharp_reach` and `sharp_note`). `agie_job` accepts only a punch that is a closed convex prism (`is_closed_convex_prism`). A convex punch has no inside corners. Thus the generator cannot leave corner material, and it cannot write the note "sharp inside corners stated" for a job that Agie accepts.
- Result: with `sharp_corners: true` the native job is the same as with `false`. The option is not relevant here. This is safe, and it is not a blocker. An optional follow-up: refuse the option by name in `agie_job`, so that the operator does not think that the control uses it.
